input.rationale: Interpretation of the margin receipt f82d709e8f5f4f80ba19cc48ff29ff0a (completed, exit_code 0) for the wedge investigation. Parsed events: peer_loss_after_wedge at indices 3 and 7 are the three-voter control and faulted steps, 15 and 16 the five-voter control steps, and 20 and 21 the five-voter faulted steps; the truncation phases precede each and re-witness the wedge. The measurement confirms the margin generalisation recorded with the investigation: the wedged replica costs exactly one unit of failure margin in both sizes. The knowledge entry for the margin behaviour is updated to the same statement with the executed observations attached.

knowledge.statement: commitment keeps one match index per voter of the current configuration and takes the quorum match index as the middle of the sorted values, so a voter whose stored log can never advance holds its slot at the stuck index for as long as the configuration stands. The wedged replica therefore consumes exactly one unit of the configuration's failure margin: the remaining voters must be able to form a quorum on their own, which in a three-voter configuration is impossible once one other voter is gone and in a five-voter configuration only becomes impossible when two other voters are gone.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; a voter whose durable log is stuck below the leader's committed prefix while it remains a member of configurations.latest; commitment.setConfiguration has been applied for that configuration.

interpretations.rationale: Five-voter control (indices 15 and 16): removing one voter still commits the applied entry (commit index 5 to 6, apply future completed with no error) and removing a second voter commits the next one as well (6 to 7, future completed), with the leader's store reaching 1..7 and the follower that takes the wedged role in the control following to the same values; the control therefore tolerates two voter losses. Five-voter faulted (indices 20 and 21): after one voter is removed the entry still commits (5 to 6, future completed) even though the wedged replica is present, but after a second removal the leader's log advances to index 7 (store 1..7, certificate (7,3)) while its commit index stays 6 in every sample of the 1500 ms window and the apply future never completes. The wedged replica's own probe is identical at both steps (store first 1, last 2, certificate (4,2), GetLog of the certificate index reporting 'log not found', StoreLogs attempts 3 and delivered 2, commit and applied 2), so its slot is frozen at the index it held before the wedge. Three-voter baseline (indices 3 and 7): the control commits after its single removal (5 to 6) while the faulted cluster stalls at the same step (commit stays 5, future never completes). Reading the two sizes together: the faulted configuration always stalls exactly one removal earlier than the healthy configuration of the same size, which is the measured form of the margin generalisation. Mechanism, source-backed: commitment takes one match index per voter of the current configuration and requires a quorum of them to reach the entry, so a voter whose durable log cannot advance keeps occupying its slot at the frozen index; the remaining voters must therefore be able to form a quorum without it. Predicate evaluated: a wedged replica must not reduce the configuration's failure margin. It is contradicted in both measured sizes, and the reduction is exactly one unit. Scope: three- and five-voter configurations, in-memory transport, deterministic single StoreLogs error, one process, escalation performed by removing voters at the transport level rather than by stopping their processes.

knowledge.assertion: A wedged replica holds one commitment slot at its stuck index and therefore consumes exactly one unit of the configuration's failure margin.
One allowed StoreLogs error after a conflicting-suffix deletion leaves the follower unable to converge, and removing the error does not restore progress.
The reject branch floors nextIndex and re-sends the same request; a snapshot is only produced from the leader's own log store.

counterevidence: The reduction is exactly the one slot the wedged replica occupies, so the finding is a margin statement rather than a claim that the wedge collapses a cluster: a five-voter cluster with a wedged replica still commits while three healthy voters answer, and even a three-voter cluster keeps committing while both other voters answer.
The control in the same execution commits in the same steps up to one removal later, so the stalled commits are not an artefact of removing transports or of the in-process harness.

The removed voters keep their membership and continue campaigning as lone candidates (visible in the earlier receipt), which did not depose the leader during the windows, so they are not a competing cause; the stall is explained by the match-index arithmetic.

The wedge itself still requires the exact combination staged here (a conflicting-suffix truncation followed by an allowed StoreLogs error), and a restart repairs it, so the margin loss persists only for an operator who neither restarts the replica nor replaces it.
limitations: Two configuration sizes were measured (three and five voters) with one or two removals respectively; the general statement 'exactly one unit' is inferred from those two sizes and the commitment arithmetic, not from every size.

The escalation removes voters by disconnecting their transports rather than stopping their processes, so the removed nodes keep running and campaigning; that does not affect the quorum arithmetic but is a difference from a real failure.
Each step was observed for 1500 ms with 25 ms sampling; a slower commit or a later snapshot-driven repair beyond the window is not claimed.
One retained execution per case, in-memory transport, deterministic fault injection on a single node, default protocol version.
interpretations.report_title: 被卡死副本确切地消耗一份故障余量：五节点集群仅能再容错一台，对照组可容错两台
interpretations.report_answer: 针对第二条发现的余量推广，本次保留执行 f82d709e8f5f4f80ba19cc48ff29ff0a 在同一套合法历史（分区、分歧、更高任期替换）上把规模参数化后得到确证：五节点对照组中，移除 1 台投票者后新条目仍提交（commit 5→6），再移除 1 台（共 2 台）后仍提交（6→7）；五节点故障组中，移除 1 台时仍能提交（5→6），再移除 1 台（共 2 台）时领导者自身日志已到 index 7（store 1..7、证书 (7,3)），但 1500 毫秒窗口内 commit 恒为 6、客户端 future 永不完成。三节点基线同样如此：对照组移除 1 台可提交，故障组移除 1 台即停摆。被卡死副本的探针在各步骤中完全不变（store last 2、证书 (4,2)、GetLog 报 log not found、StoreLogs 尝试次数停 3）。结论：卡死副本的承诺槽位被冻结在旧下标，因此确切消耗一份故障余量——三节点集群失去单点容错，五节点集群从『可容错两台』降为『仅能容错一台』；该余量损失持续到该副本被重启（同盘重启已证实可修复）或被替换为止。缺陷主张维持，余量结论以两种规模与提交法定人数算术为依据。

knowledge.statement: For an explicit leadership transfer (LeadershipTransferToServer) the leader accepts the caller-supplied target if and only if a followerReplication entry exists for that ServerID in leaderState.replState; the only rejection is a target equal to the local ID ('cannot transfer leadership to itself'). No suffrage test is applied at the API, at initiateLeadershipTransfer, or at the leaderLoop hand-off to leadershipTransfer.
knowledge.conditions: protocolVersion >= 3, node is in Leader state and processing the leadershipTransferCh case on the main thread; the caller supplies an ID present in configurations.latest.

knowledge.statement: startStopReplication starts a followerReplication goroutine for every server in configurations.latest whose ID differs from the local ID, with no suffrage filter, so leaderState.replState (the map consulted by the explicit transfer path and by pickServer) also contains Nonvoter members. pickServer, by contrast, skips 'server.Suffrage != Voter', so the targetless transfer path cannot select a non-voter.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state, after appendConfigurationEntry/setLatestConfiguration followed by startStopReplication.

knowledge.statement: On receiving a TimeoutNowRequest a node clears its known leader, sets its state to Candidate and sets candidateFromLeadershipTransfer to true, then acknowledges. The handler performs no term comparison (TimeoutNowRequest carries no term), no state check, no suffrage check on the receiver, and no check that the sender is the current leader or a configuration member; runCandidate then skips pre-vote for such a candidate and calls electSelf directly.
knowledge.conditions: The RPC passes checkRPCHeader (protocol version range) and is dispatched from processRPC on the main thread.

knowledge.statement: In requestVote, when a RequestVote arrives with req.Term > currentTerm the receiver first steps down (setState(Follower)) and adopts the higher term, and only afterwards rejects the request because the candidate is not a Voter ('rejecting vote request since node is not a voter'), returning Granted false. Because the step-down precedes the rejection, a term-advancing vote request from an unelectable candidate still removes the receiver from leadership.
knowledge.conditions: Receiver is a Voter or Leader with a non-empty configurations.latest.Servers, and the candidate passes the inConfiguration check.

knowledge.statement: In appendEntries, when a received entry conflicts with one the node already stores, the node deletes the range [entry.Index, lastLogIdx] via logs.DeleteRange, then stores the replacement entries via logs.StoreLogs. If StoreLogs returns an error the handler logs 'failed to append to logs' and returns before any setLastLog call: the in-memory lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm keep the values they had before the deletion (the code marks this with a TODO), and no other branch in the receive path restores them. The response for that request is left with Success false.
knowledge.conditions: Follower/Candidate state; a.Term not older than the node's current term; at least one received entry whose index is at or below the node's last log index and whose term differs from the stored entry; and an error return from logs.StoreLogs for that call.

knowledge.statement: The in-memory last-log certificate is read through raftState.getLastEntry (and getLastIndex, which takes the maximum of lastLogIndex and lastSnapshotIndex, so a snapshot does not mask a stale log index). Its consumers are: electSelf and preElectSelf, which put it in RequestVoteRequest/RequestPreVoteRequest as LastLogIndex/LastLogTerm; requestVote/requestPreVote, which use it to decide whether to grant a vote; appendEntries, which compares it against PrevLogEntry to validate a leader's previous entry; and Raft.LastIndex, the public accessor. None of these consult the LogStore.
knowledge.conditions: Any node, whenever it campaigns or answers a vote request or validates an AppendEntries previous entry.

knowledge.statement: In the appendEntries entry loop the comparison 'entry.Index > lastLogIdx' uses lastLogIdx read from the in-memory certificate (getLastLog), not from the log store. For an entry at or below that cached index the handler calls logs.GetLog(entry.Index) and returns immediately if it errors, so once the conflicting suffix has been deleted from the store, any re-sent entry covering those indices makes the handler return before StoreLogs is reached. The certificate is never re-derived from the store inside this handler.
knowledge.conditions: Follower or Candidate state with at least one entry in the request whose index is at or below the cached last log index while that index is absent from the store (the state produced by a failed StoreLogs immediately after a conflicting-suffix deletion).

knowledge.statement: On an unsuccessful AppendEntries response the leader sets the peer's nextIndex to max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1), 1). When the follower's response carries a LastLog at or above the leader's index, the value settles at 1 (or at the floor) and the leader re-sends the same request, so a follower that rejects for a self-inflicted reason is re-driven with an identical request rather than a snapshot; ErrLogNotFound leading to SEND_SNAP is only produced from the leader's own log store, not from the follower's response.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; the follower responds Success=false with a LastLog hint at or above the leader's last index.

knowledge.statement: A single allowed error return from LogStore.StoreLogs in the call that follows a conflicting-suffix deletion leaves the follower unable to converge: its durable log keeps the truncated state (its last index falls to the last surviving index before the conflict), its cached last-log certificate keeps describing the deleted suffix, its commit and applied indexes stop advancing, and no further StoreLogs call is even attempted, so removing the error afterwards does not restore progress.
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter cluster over an in-memory transport, one follower holding an isolated uncommitted tail appended at an earlier term, a higher-term leader with committed replacement entries at the same indices, and exactly one allowed StoreLogs error on the replacement write; the fault may be removed afterwards without changing the outcome. In the observed run the same history with a healthy store converged inside the window (store 1..5, certificate (5,3), commit and applied 5) while the faulted node stayed at store last 2, certificate (4,2) and commit and applied 2 for 2.7 s.

knowledge.statement: When the wedged replica from the conflict-truncation store-error state is one of three voters, the cluster cannot commit any new entry after a single further voter loss: the leader accepts the entry into its own log (store and certificate advance to the new index) but its commit index stays at the value it had before and the client's apply future never completes, whereas the control run of the identical history without the store error commits the same entry as soon as the peer-loss phase begins. The wedged replica's store last index and StoreLogs attempt counter are unchanged across the phase, so its match index cannot advance and the quorum of match indexes can no longer include the new entry.
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter cluster over an in-memory transport; one voter left in the conflict-truncation store-error state (store truncated, cached certificate stale, no further store writes); one further voter removed; one client entry applied on the remaining leader. Observed for 1500 ms with 25 ms sampling, with the matching control run in the same execution.

knowledge.statement: appendConfigurationEntry dispatches the configuration entry and then, without waiting for it to commit, sets configurations.latest to the new configuration and calls leaderState.commitment.setConfiguration, which rebuilds the match-index map so that every voter of the new configuration is counted, with servers that have never answered starting at 0. The quorum decisions for commitment therefore use the new configuration from that moment, while configurations.committed still describes the old one.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; any successful configuration change request (AddVoter, AddNonvoter, DemoteVoter, RemoveServer) whose entry has been appended but not yet committed.

knowledge.statement: Both the leader lease check and the election path read configurations.latest, not the committed configuration: checkLeaderLease counts contacted voters of the latest configuration and demotes the leader when that count is below the latest configuration's quorum size, and quorumSize (used by candidates to decide when they have won) is computed from the same latest configuration. An uncommitted configuration whose quorum requires a server that never answers therefore both blocks commitment and removes the surviving servers' ability to keep or regain leadership.
knowledge.conditions: A node whose configurations.latest includes a voter added by a configuration entry that has not committed, while that voter is unreachable.

knowledge.statement: The timeout accepted by the configuration-change APIs bounds only the attempt to hand the request to the main loop: requestConfigChange returns errorFuture{ErrEnqueueTimeout} if the timer fires before the request is queued, otherwise it returns the future whose Error blocks until the configuration entry commits. A caller cannot use that timeout to learn that the configuration change is stuck.
knowledge.conditions: Any AddVoter/AddNonvoter/DemoteVoter/RemoveServer call with a non-zero timeout.

knowledge.statement: On a single-voter cluster, AddVoter for a server that is not running yet commits the configuration change (the leader's own match is recorded against the previous configuration's quorum) and the future completes successfully, after which the only node loses leadership within the lease timeout and remains a Candidate that cannot be re-elected under the configuration it just committed, so client writes are refused with ErrNotLeader until the named server appears; pre-vote keeps its term unchanged throughout, and starting the named server restores leadership.
knowledge.conditions: Protocol version 3, a configuration with exactly one voter grown by one voter (so the new configuration's quorum cannot be met by the surviving server), the named server not running, no faults, in-memory transport. Observed with 25 ms sampling for 1500 ms after the call, with the same call on an equivalent cluster whose named server was already running as the control.

knowledge.statement: A wedged replica (conflict-truncation store-error state) does not converge while running, even after the store error is removed, but a restart over the same durable state does converge: after restarting the same stores with a fresh transport at the same address, the certificate, the store's last index and the commit index return to the leader's values and the leader's re-sent entries are stored (certificate (5,3) versus the wedged (4,2), commit 0 to 5).
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter cluster, in-memory transport, the store wrapper's error no longer injected; restart modelled as NewRaft over the same log store, stable store and snapshot store with a new transport at the same address and the peers rewired (Shutdown closes the transport it was built with). Observed for four seconds after the restart with 200 ms sampling.

The wedged replica therefore consumes exactly one unit of the configuration's failure margin: the remaining voters must be able to form a quorum on their own, which in a three-voter configuration is impossible once one other voter is gone and in a five-voter configuration only becomes impossible when two other voters are gone.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; a voter whose durable log is stuck below the leader's committed prefix while it remains a member of configurations.latest; commitment.setConfiguration has been applied for that configuration.

interpretations.rationale: Admission (index 2): a leader elected at term 2 holds configurations.latest = 3 Voters (server-2b9dbd0a, server-f1a6871a, server-2c19f1a0) plus 1 Nonvoter (server-752e4a42, target_id) added through the public AddNonvoter API; the target had learned the 4-server configuration and had caught up to the freshly committed proof entry (target_last_index 4, target_commit_index 4, target_caught_up_to_proof true), and target_is_voter_on_leader is false. Transfer request (index 3): LeadershipTransferToServer(server-752e4a42) returned nil after 0.23 ms, i.e. the API reported success. Observed vote campaign: three RequestVoteRequests were received by each of the three voters (server-2c19f1a0, server-2b9dbd0a, server-f1a6871a) at t_ms 0.228/0.316/0.318 with candidate_id server-752e4a42 (the non-voter target), term 3 (= the pre-transfer term + 1), last_log_index 4 / last_log_term 2 (the leader's own log position, so the log-freshness test passed) and transfer_flagged true. Observed effects: the incumbent server-f1a6871a left Leader at t_ms 0.319 and ended the window as Follower at term 4; the target was sampled as Candidate at t_ms 0.231 and then Follower at t_ms 68.9, never Leader; no node was Leader immediately after (leaders_after shows only the newly elected server-2b9dbd0a, at term 4, elected at t_ms 67.5-69.0). Recovery poll (index 4): at t_ms 512 the three voters hold exactly one leader (server-2b9dbd0a, term 4) and the non-voter target is a Follower at term 4. Control (indices 0-1): the identical call to a Voter target (server-b1cc7b19) returned nil after 0.33 ms and the named target became Leader at term 3 at t_ms 0.36, with the same transfer_flagged vote request witnessed. The two executions differ only in the target's suffrage, so the outcome is attributable to eligibility, not to generic transfer flakiness. Mechanism, all source-backed: the transfer path accepts the target because replState holds an entry for non-voters (raft.go 587); TimeoutNow has no term, state or suffrage test, so the non-voter campaigns at term+1 (2208-2215); every voter adopts that higher term and steps down before rejecting the candidate as a non-voter (1670-1683); and the candidate can obtain no grant because electSelf only asks and self-votes Voters (2015). Consequences: (a) a documented public API call (api.go 1275-1284, a specific server in the cluster) destroys the incumbent's leadership and produces no transfer to the named target; (b) the returned future reports success (nil), so the caller cannot distinguish a completed transfer from a deposed leader; (c) the API doc promises that an unpromotable follower will fail gracefully, which is contradicted by the observed deposition. The deposition is not merely an unobserved side effect: it is the direct consequence of the source-visible step-down-before-reject order, and the target's inability to win is structural while it remains a Nonvoter in every voter's latest configuration, not a sampling artifact. Scope: leadership transfer (protocol version >= 3) on a leader whose latest configuration contains a non-voter member, initiated with the caller-supplied ID of that member; observed with in-memory transport, no faults, one process.

knowledge.assertion: The explicit transfer path accepts the target on replication-state existence alone and rejects only a self-target.
leaderState.replState contains Nonvoter members, so a non-voter target passes that check.
TimeoutNow puts any receiver into candidacy with the transfer flag and no term, state or suffrage test.
A voter adopts the higher term and steps down before rejecting a non-voter candidate, so the term-advancing request deposes it.

counterevidence: No safety violation was observed: no two leaders, no committed entry was lost, the target's transfer-flagged request was rejected by voters with the explicit 'rejecting vote request since node is not a voter' branch, and the three voters had exactly one leader again about 69 ms after the call.

The voters' step-down on a higher-term vote request is deliberate library behaviour for a demoted node that campaigns (the comment cites hashicorp/raft#526), so one may describe the deposition as an anticipated consequence of that branch rather than as an oversight in it.

The scenario requires the caller to name a non-voter: the targetless LeadershipTransfer() cannot select one, because pickServer skips servers whose Suffrage is not Voter, so the trigger is caller-supplied rather than internally produced.
limitations: One retained execution, one process, in-memory LoopbackTransport, no faults, and non-default short timeouts (heartbeat/election/lease 50 ms, commit 5 ms); the unavailability interval therefore scales with the configured ElectionTimeout and the measured 69 ms is not a production figure.

'The target never becomes Leader' is asserted for the sampled window (500 ms) plus the recovery poll and is structurally supported while the target remains a Nonvoter; it is not a claim about every future configuration (a concurrent promotion would change eligibility).

The future's nil value is the library's documented 'lost leadership during transfer (expected)' path; the finding rests on the combination of that success value with the absence of the named transfer and the incumbent's deposition, not on the nil value alone.

Native local feedback in a scratch copy inside the draft showed the same pattern with the incumbent re-electing itself rather than another voter becoming leader (schedule-dependent), but that run is not retained evidence and is not relied on.
interpretations.report_title: 显式领导权转移接受不可当选的非投票者目标：现任领导者被罢免、转移未发生，而 future 仍返回成功
interpretations.report_answer: 已确认的有源缺陷：Hashicorp Raft（本快照）的 LeadershipTransferToServer 路径只检查目标是否为自己、是否存在复制状态，未检查目标在最新配置中是否为 Voter。当一个由公开 AddNonvoter 加入且已追平日志的成员被指定为目标时：TimeoutNow（无 term、无状态、无选举权校验）使该非投票者在 term+1 发起选举；各投票者先接受更高任期并下台，随后以“candidate 非投票者”为由拒绝投票，因此目标永远无法当选。保留执行（79cf4ec11d694dfbaeb78ac8b07e1f67）显示：转移 future 在 0.23 毫秒后返回 nil（成功），目标从未成为 Leader，原领导者在 0.32 毫秒内失去领导权，约 69 毫秒后由另一名投票者当选；同一 API 对投票者目标的对照调用则真正完成转移。即：一次合法的公开 API 调用会罢免现任领导者、不产生所指名的转移，且调用方无法从返回值得知失败。

interpretations.rationale: Admission (index 3): the diverging node was elected leader first (its log was 1..4 with 1..2 committed, and 3..4 appended at term 2 while it was isolated, certificate (4,2)); the majority elected a leader at term 3 and committed entries 3..5 (its store held 1..5 with commit 5). The wrapper shows the diverging node had made exactly two successful StoreLogs calls up to that point, so the next StoreLogs on that node is the one belonging to the conflicting-suffix replacement. Faulted case after the heal (index 4): the store's last index drops from 4 to 2 within the first samples (the deletion removed 3..4) and stays 2 for the rest of the 1500 ms window, while the node's cached certificate stays (4,2) and GetLog of the certificate index returns 'log not found'; commit_index and applied_index stay at 2, the values they had before the heal; the StoreLogs attempt counter rises exactly once, from 2 to 3, and never moves again, so the follower never reaches the store again even though the leader keeps sending; the node stays a Follower at term 3 while the leader holds store 1..5 with commit 5. The library's own output in the same receipt records both halves of the cycle: 'failed to get log entry: index=3 error=...' from the follower's entry loop, and the leader's 'appendEntries rejected, sending older logs ... next=2' followed by '... next=1' and a further '... next=1', that is, the nextIndex floor with the identical request re-sent. After the fault was removed (index 5, 1200 ms later) nothing changes: certificate (4,2), store 1..2, attempts still 3, commit and applied still 2. Control, the same history with a healthy store (index 1): the store's last index moves from 4 to 5, the certificate moves from (4,2) to (5,3), the attempt counter moves from 2 to 4, GetLog of the certificate index succeeds and commit and applied reach 5. The two runs differ only in whether that single StoreLogs call returned an error, so the cause is the interaction of the allowed store error with the receive path rather than the divergence, the election or the heal. Predicate evaluated: an allowed LogStore error during a conflicting-suffix replacement must not prevent the node from converging once the fault ends. It is contradicted by a valid witness: across 2.7 s of continuing leader retries the node's durable log never regains indices 3..4 and no further StoreLogs is attempted. Mechanism, source-backed: the entry loop decides whether an incoming entry is already stored by comparing it with the cached last log index and then reading it from the store, so the just-deleted indices make GetLog fail and the handler returns before StoreLogs; the certificate that would have been updated is never re-derived; and the leader's reject branch floors nextIndex at 1 and re-sends the same request, restoring the blocking state instead of repairing it, while SEND_SNAP is never reached because ErrLogNotFound is only produced from the leader's own log store. Scope: one follower in a three-voter cluster over an in-memory transport, after a legal partition, divergence and higher-term replacement history, with a single allowed StoreLogs error, observed for 2.7 s with the fault both armed and removed.

knowledge.assertion: The conflict path deletes the suffix, then stores replacements, and an error return skips the certificate update.
The cached certificate is what electSelf, requestVote, appendEntries and LastIndex read; none consult the log store.
The entry loop compares against the cached last index and returns on a GetLog error for entries that were just deleted, before reaching StoreLogs.
The leader's reject branch floors the peer's nextIndex and re-sends the same request; ErrLogNotFound leading to a snapshot only comes from the leader's own log store.

counterevidence: Safety is not violated in this history: the leader and the other follower kept a quorum and continued committing (store 1..5, commit 5), the wedged node's tail entries were appended in isolation and never committed, and no two leaders appeared.

Cluster-level liveness continues in the observed window; the defect is a per-replica progress failure, so the severity depends on remaining redundancy - with the third voter down the wedged replica cannot serve as quorum for anything past index 2.

The trigger needs an exact window, a conflicting-suffix truncation followed immediately by an error return from StoreLogs, and the fault-injecting wrapper reproduces it deterministically, so its real-world frequency is a separate empirical question.

The condition is visible outside the library: the run's output shows repeated 'failed to get log entry' warnings from the follower and 'appendEntries rejected, sending older logs ... next=1' from the leader, and a process restart would rebuild the certificate from the store.
limitations: Scope of the word permanently here is the observed interval with no in-library repair enabled: 1500 ms with the fault armed plus 1200 ms after it was removed, during which the store never advanced. The claim rests on the mechanism, entries below the cached index are never stored again and the certificate is never re-derived, not on infinite execution.

No InstallSnapshot and no restart were performed, so the source-derived statement that those are the only repairs stays unexecuted; neither the leader-side compaction that would force a snapshot nor the restart path was reached.

One retained execution, one process, in-memory transport, three voters, default protocol version and deterministic fault injection; the wrapper returns an error without touching the underlying store, which the interface permits but which is not a model of a real disk failure.
The account uses 25 ms state probes plus the library's own log lines, so intermediate transitions shorter than the sampling interval are not claimed.
interpretations.report_title: 截断后一次合法的 StoreLogs 错误会永久卡死该跟随者的日志复制
interpretations.report_answer: 已确认的有源缺陷（A1 进度 / A2 上下文）：跟随者处理与自身后缀冲突的条目时，先删除冲突后缀、再写入替换条目；若这次写入返回合法的存储错误，处理器会在更新内存中的 last log 证书之前返回。由于条目循环用『缓存的 last index』判断条目是否已存在、再去存储读取，被删除的下标已不存在，GetLog 失败让处理器再次提前返回：替换条目永远写不进去，证书也永不被重算。保留执行 2086b09f107d4d49b1407754feabb781 显示：注入一次合法 StoreLogs 错误后，该节点存储最后下标由 4 降到 2（3、4 被删除且未写回），缓存证书停在 (4,2)（对证书下标的 GetLog 报 log not found），commit/applied 停在 2，StoreLogs 尝试次数仅由 2 增至 3 后不再增长；领导者侧日志显示其拒绝重试并把 nextIndex 降到 1 后反复重发同一请求。把故障移除后再等 1200 毫秒仍无任何进展；而完全相同的历史在健康存储下（对照组）1.5 秒内收敛：存储 1..5、证书 (5,3)、commit/applied 均为 5。即一次合法的存储写失败就把该副本永久移出复制集合，只有进程重启或安装快照才能修复，而本库中没有任何路径会因该状态触发这两者。

interpretations.rationale: The faulted peer-loss phase (index 7) removes one of the three voters, the single failure a three-voter configuration is expected to absorb, and then applies one new client entry on the leader. Observations: the leader stays Leader at term 3, its own log reaches index 6 (store 1..6, certificate (6,3)) but its commit index is 5 in all 58 samples across the 1500 ms window, its applied index stays 5, and the returned apply future never completes (apply_future_done false). The wedge is still present in the same phase: the wedged node's store last index is 2, its certificate is (4,2), GetLog of that index returns 'log not found' and its StoreLogs attempt counter is still 3, i.e. unchanged from the earlier receipt. The removed voter sits as a Candidate at term 3, as an isolated node should. The control peer-loss phase (index 3) is the same step without the store error: the leader commits immediately (commit index moves 5 to 6 in the first samples, applied 6, apply_future_done true with no error), and the converged node follows to store 1..6 with certificate (6,3). The two phases differ only in whether the StoreLogs error happened earlier in the history, so the stalled commit is attributable to the wedge rather than to removing a voter, to the leader, or to the harness. Mechanism, source-backed: commitment needs a quorum of match indexes, the wedged replica can never match past index 2 because its entry loop returns before storing anything at or below its cached last index, so once the third voter is gone the quorum of match indexes can no longer reach the new entry even though the leader holds it; the leader's own log and store advance, which is why the client's write is accepted and then never completed. The advertised consequence is therefore availability, not safety: no committed entry is lost, and the same execution shows no two leaders and no divergence of the surviving nodes. Predicate evaluated: a three-voter cluster with one voter removed must still be able to commit a new entry. It is contradicted by a valid witness in the faulted mode and satisfied in the control, so the wedge converts one allowed store error into a permanent loss of the configuration's one-failure tolerance for writes until the wedged replica is restarted or receives a snapshot.

knowledge.assertion: One allowed StoreLogs error after a conflicting-suffix deletion leaves the follower unable to converge, and removing the error does not restore progress.
The entry loop returns on a GetLog error for entries at or below the cached last index, before reaching StoreLogs.
The reject branch floors nextIndex and re-sends the same request; a snapshot is only produced from the leader's own log store.

counterevidence: The unavailable capability is write availability, not safety: the leader stayed Leader, no committed entry was lost, and the control shows the same cluster shape committing normally, so nothing in the observation contradicts linearizability of what was already committed.

The stall is bounded by operational repair: a restart of the wedged node rebuilds its certificate from its store (NewRaft reads the log store) and an InstallSnapshot restores it, and this experiment executed neither, so the observed interval is 1500 ms of retries rather than a proof of permanence.

The removed voter is isolated rather than stopped, so its own election attempts continued (observed as Candidate at term 3); that did not make the leader step down, so it is not a competing cause for the stalled commit, but it is a difference from a real process failure.
Both modes in the same execution used the deterministic fault wrapper, so the trigger frequency in a deployment with a real store error remains an empirical question.
limitations: The availability claim is measured inside one 1500 ms window with 25 ms sampling in one execution; it rests on the mechanism (a wedged replica's match index cannot advance) plus the control, not on an unlimited observation.
Only a three-voter configuration was exercised, so the statement covers the loss of the one-failure tolerance there; how a five-voter cluster degrades was not measured.
Neither restart nor snapshot install was executed, so their role as the only repairs stays source-derived; likewise no leader-side compaction was reached.
The stage used an in-memory transport, one process and default protocol version, and the fault wrapper returns an error without touching the underlying store.
interpretations.joint_history: Both receipts are produced by the same harness file in the same workspace: the successor run's basis is the draft harness with the peer-loss escalation phase appended, and the truncation subtests it contains are byte-identical in behaviour to the ones the predecessor ran. The successor therefore re-witnesses the fault-injected truncation history on a fresh process (its indices 4, 5 and 6 correspond to the predecessor's 3, 4 and 5: same staging, same fault wrapper, same probes), which is why the predecessor remains valid as the original witness for the convergence result while the successor is the witness for the escalation. The two are separate complete executions with independent sampling; neither's observation depends on the other's output, and the comparison inside the successor (its own control subtests at indices 0, 1 and the control peer-loss phase at index 3) is self-contained. The shared identity across the two receipts is the harness lineage plus the staged history (three voters, isolated initial leader, higher-term replacement, one injected StoreLogs error), not a claim that one execution's bytes continue in the other.
interpretations.report_title: 被卡死的副本使三节点集群失去单点故障容忍：一次合法的 StoreLogs 错误后无法再提交任何新日志
interpretations.report_answer: 在既有发现（截断窗口内一次合法的 StoreLogs 错误会永久卡死该跟随者）之上，本次保留执行 afeb14d0d23e445d8383bb535f0c0e64 追加了可用的后果并得到确证：故障模式下，移除三名投票者中的一名（三节点配置本应容忍的一次故障）后，领导者仍为 Leader（term 3），自身日志已到 index 6（store 1..6、证书 (6,3)），但 commit index 在整个 1500 毫秒窗口的 58 次采样中恒为 5，applied 停在 5，客户端写入的 future 始终未完成；被卡死副本仍是 store last=2、证书 (4,2)、StoreLogs 尝试次数停在 3。同一执行中的对照（相同历史但不注入存储错误）在移除同一名投票者后立即提交成功（commit 5→6、applied 6、future 以 nil 完成）。机制与源码一致：提交需要匹配索引的多数派，而卡死副本永远不会再把任何条目写入存储（其条目循环在 GetLog 失败处提前返回），因此当第三个投票者消失时，匹配索引无法达到新的条目。结论：一次合法的存储写错误就把该集群的单点故障容忍度降为零（写不可用），直到重启该副本或安装快照；这不影响安全性（无已提交条目丢失、未出现双 Leader），但属于明确有界的活性缺陷。

interpretations.rationale: Admission (index 8): a real single-voter cluster, leader at term 2 with commit index 2 and last index 2, its configuration listing only itself, and the named second server's identity derived from a transport that is not wired to the cluster and has no raft running (named_server_up false); the configuration entry will be index 3. Window (index 9): the commit index moves from 2 to 3 within the first samples, so the configuration entry does commit, and the AddVoter future completes with no error (future_resolved true, future_error null). This contradicts the prediction recorded with the question that the configuration entry could not commit: dispatchLogs calls commitment.match for the leader before appendConfigurationEntry installs the new configuration, so the entry is matched under the previous single-voter quorum and committed, and only afterwards does the new configuration govern. What follows is nonetheless the predicted consequence: the sampled state is Leader for the first three samples, then Follower, then Candidate for the remaining samples; the node stays a Candidate at term 2 for the whole window (term_samples contains only 2), because pre-vote does not advance the term, and it cannot win anyway since the new configuration's quorum is two and only one server answers. Client work (index 10) is refused with 'node is not the leader' and the commit index stays 3: the cluster, which in this configuration is the only node, has no leader and no further progress. Recovery (index 11): as soon as the named server is started at its announced address and wired in, the original node wins at term 3 and becomes Leader again with the named node following, so the state is repairable by the event the caller controls. Control (indices 12-15): with the named server running before the call, the leader stays Leader in all 59 samples, the commit index reaches 3, a client write succeeds (write_error null, commit 4) and the growth completes normally. The two cases differ only in whether the named server was already running, so the absent server is the cause. Corrected account: following the sequence BootstrapCluster's documentation recommends (bootstrap one voter, then AddVoter the next server) makes the cluster unavailable when the next server has not been started yet, and the API reports success because the configuration change itself commits. The harm is availability, not safety: no committed entry is lost, and the single node never splits into two leaders. Predicate evaluated: following the documented growth sequence with the next server not yet running must not remove the ability to serve, or must at least be reported as a failure by the API that performed it. It is contradicted by the witness: the AddVoter future reports success while the only node loses leadership, cannot be re-elected under the configuration it just committed, and refuses client writes with ErrNotLeader. Scope: configuration version 3, a single-voter configuration grown by one voter, the new configuration's quorum (2 of 2) therefore requiring the new server, no faults, one process, in-memory transport.
counterevidence: The recorded prediction that the configuration entry cannot commit is refuted by this receipt: commit_index reaches the configuration entry's index before the leader steps down, because the leader's own match is recorded against the previous configuration's quorum. The defect account is corrected accordingly; the unavailability comes from the lease quorum and from the election quorum of the committed configuration, not from an uncommitted entry.

Recovery is automatic and caller-controlled: starting the named server restores leadership within the same execution (index 11), so the harm window ends when the operator performs the step the sequence implies.

The safe alternatives exist inside the library: AddNonvoter first (non-voters receive log entries without counting for quorum) and AddVoter only when the server is up, or start the server before AddVoter as the control does. The defect is therefore about the documented sequence and the successful API result, not about a missing capability.

The named server's absence is the caller's input; the audit-relevant part is that the library's own documentation recommends this ordering and still describes AddVoter as adding a staging server that is promoted once ready.
limitations: One retained execution, one process, in-memory transport, one configuration shape (1 to 2 voters) and short timeouts; in the observed run the loss of leadership happened about 75 ms after the call (three samples) and the window measured 1500 ms, so the production duration scales with LeaderLeaseTimeout and then lasts as long as the named server is absent.

Only the 1-to-2 growth step is exercised here; the same step from two or more voters keeps a quorum among the survivors, so the finding is scoped to that step and to any configuration whose new quorum cannot be met without the absent server.

The control is a separate single-voter cluster built later in the same execution rather than the same cluster with the server present, so the comparison is between equivalent configurations rather than the same cluster instance.

The documentation statements are treated as normative source text, not as an enforced contract; the code has no check that the named server is reachable, and the deprecation of the Staging suffrage left the AddVoter documentation describing behaviour that the code no longer implements.
interpretations.report_title: 按库自身文档的顺序扩展单节点集群会让集群失去领导者：AddVoter 报告成功却拒绝写入
interpretations.report_answer: 已确认的有源缺陷（A1 进度 / A2 成员与权限）：BootstrapCluster 的文档建议先以单个 Voter 引导、再用 AddVoter 加入其他服务器，而 AddVoter 的文档仍沿用旧的 staging 语义（加入后『待其就绪再提升为 Voter』）。本快照中 AddVoter 会立即把目标写入最新配置并作为 Voter 生效。保留执行 e19ad6d076fa4d878b7bd0f90f067fca 显示：在真实单节点集群上对一台尚未启动的服务器调用 AddVoter 后，该配置项在旧配置的法定人数下立即提交（commit 2→3），AddVoter future 返回 nil（成功）；但随后唯一的节点被降为 Follower、再变为 Candidate ——状态采样为 Leader×3 → Follower → Candidate，整个 1500 毫秒窗口内 term 恒为 2（预投票避免了任期膨胀），之后客户端写入被拒（node is not the leader），commit 停在上限。也就是说：整个（单节点）集群在命名服务器出现之前不可用，而触发它的 API 却报告成功；一旦该服务器在其地址上启动，集群自动恢复（原节点在 term 3 重新当选）。对照实验（同一调用，但服务器已先启动）则全程保持 Leader、写入成功。该缺陷是可用性问题而非安全性问题（无已提交条目丢失、无双 Leader），但文档所推荐的扩展顺序与实际行为相矛盾，且 safe 路径（先 AddNonvoter、就绪后再 AddVoter 提升）在库中存在却未被文档指引。

interpretations.rationale: Before the restart (index 9, and still true after the fault was removed at index 10) the wedged node shows exactly the state the earlier receipts recorded: store last index 2 while the certificate is (4,2), GetLog of the certificate index returns 'log not found', the StoreLogs attempt counter is 3 and does not move for the whole 1500 ms window even though the leader's certificate and store hold 1..5, and commit and applied stay at 2. The leader is unchanged at term 3 with commit 5, so the wedge is not a leader-side artefact. After the restart (index 11) the node is rebuilt on the same log store, stable store and snapshot store with a new transport at the same address: the certificate index samples move from 2 to 5 and the store's last index moves from 2 to 5, the commit index moves from 0 to 5, applied reaches 5, the certificate is (5,3) with GetLog of that index succeeding, and the store's attempt/delivery counters advance from 3/2 to 5/4, so the leader's re-sent entries were stored. Convergence happened about 1.8 s after the restart (sample 9 of 20 at 200 ms), which matches the in-memory transport's 500 ms RPC timeout plus backoff for the call that was in flight when Shutdown closed the old transport, and the peers had to be rewired to the new transport because Shutdown closes the transport it was built with. Interpretation of the comparison: the predicate 'a process restart over the same durable state repairs the replica' holds, and 'the running replica repairs itself once the store error stops' does not, which is what the earlier source-derived boundary predicted. This closes the earlier limitation that no restart had been executed; it does not change the wedge defect, which stays asserted for the conditions recorded in the earlier receipts.

knowledge.assertion: One allowed StoreLogs error after a conflicting-suffix deletion leaves the follower unable to converge, and removing the error does not restore progress.
The entry loop returns on a GetLog error for entries at or below the cached last index, before reaching StoreLogs.

counterevidence: The restart repairs the state, so the wedge is not permanent in the presence of an operator restart; the defect's harm is bounded by the operational repair, and this receipt is evidence for the repair rather than for the harm.

Convergence after the restart took about 1.8 s here, but that duration is a property of the harness (in-memory transport timeout plus the leader's retry backoff after the transport was closed by Shutdown), so it is not a recovery-time claim for real deployments.
The observation window after the restart was four seconds and the state was consistent from the ninth sample on; no longer-running behaviour is claimed.

The restart was performed by the harness with the library's own constructor, not by an external process manager, so the modelled restart differs from a real process death in that the same store object was reused rather than reopened from disk.
limitations: One retained execution with deterministic fault injection, three voters, in-memory transport, short timeouts and a hand-modelled restart (fresh transport at the same address, NewRaft over the same stores).
InstallSnapshot, the other source-derived repair path, was still not executed, and no leader-side compaction was reached, so the set of repairs is confirmed only for the restart path.

The wedge evidence itself lives in the earlier receipts; this receipt re-witnesses it (indices 5, 6, 9, 10) under the same staging, and the joint history is the same harness lineage with the restart subtest added.
interpretations.joint_history: This receipt comes from the same harness file, with the same staging and the same fault wrapper as the earlier wedge receipts, extended by a third subtest that restarts the node; its control and faulted subtests re-witness the same histories on a fresh process (indices 1, 2, 5, 6, 9, 10 correspond to the earlier receipts' truncation and disarm phases), and its sampling is independent of the earlier receipts.
interpretations.report_title: 卡死副本的修复边界已被执行验证：运行中的副本不会自愈，同盘重启可以
interpretations.report_answer: 针对第二条发现（截断窗口内一次合法 StoreLogs 错误会永久卡死该跟随者）此前遗留的『未执行重启/快照修复路径』限制，本次保留执行 3cd95c2fbd4a4d9ea2eea73f1f9f4b3e 补上了边界证据：注入错误后，运行中的副本在 1500 毫秒窗口内以及移除故障后再等 1200 毫秒都无任何进展（store last 仍为 2、证书仍为 (4,2)、对证书下标的 GetLog 报 log not found、StoreLogs 尝试次数停在 3、commit/applied 停在 2，而领导者侧为 1..5、commit 5）；随后在同一份持久状态（同一 log store/stable store/snapshot store，同地址新 transport，Shutdown 会关闭旧 transport，故对端需重新接线）上重启该节点后，证书与存储在下标 2→5、commit 0→5，最终证书 (5,3)、GetLog 成功、StoreLogs 计数 3/2→5/4，即重启修复成功。结论：该缺陷的修复边界得到执行确认——运行中的副本不会自愈，同盘重启可以；约 1.8 秒的恢复延迟是本地测试设施（500 毫秒 RPC 超时 + 重试退避）的产物，不作为生产恢复时间。缺陷主张维持不变，InstallSnapshot 路径仍未执行。

result.summary: Interpreted the margin receipt: the five-voter control kept committing after two voter removals (5→6→7) while the faulted five-voter cluster committed after one and stalled at the second (log 7, commit pinned at 6, future never completing), and the three-voter baseline stalled one removal earlier than its control; conclusion violated, defect asserted, and the margin behavior knowledge now carries the executed observations.

knowledge.statement: For an explicit leadership transfer (LeadershipTransferToServer) the leader accepts the caller-supplied target if and only if a followerReplication entry exists for that ServerID in leaderState.replState; the only rejection is a target equal to the local ID ('cannot transfer leadership to itself'). No suffrage test is applied at the API, at initiateLeadershipTransfer, or at the leaderLoop hand-off to leadershipTransfer.
knowledge.conditions: protocolVersion >= 3, node is in Leader state and processing the leadershipTransferCh case on the main thread; the caller supplies an ID present in configurations.latest.

knowledge.statement: startStopReplication starts a followerReplication goroutine for every server in configurations.latest whose ID differs from the local ID, with no suffrage filter, so leaderState.replState (the map consulted by the explicit transfer path and by pickServer) also contains Nonvoter members. pickServer, by contrast, skips 'server.Suffrage != Voter', so the targetless transfer path cannot select a non-voter.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state, after appendConfigurationEntry/setLatestConfiguration followed by startStopReplication.

knowledge.statement: On receiving a TimeoutNowRequest a node clears its known leader, sets its state to Candidate and sets candidateFromLeadershipTransfer to true, then acknowledges. The handler performs no term comparison (TimeoutNowRequest carries no term), no state check, no suffrage check on the receiver, and no check that the sender is the current leader or a configuration member; runCandidate then skips pre-vote for such a candidate and calls electSelf directly.
knowledge.conditions: The RPC passes checkRPCHeader (protocol version range) and is dispatched from processRPC on the main thread.

knowledge.statement: In requestVote, when a RequestVote arrives with req.Term > currentTerm the receiver first steps down (setState(Follower)) and adopts the higher term, and only afterwards rejects the request because the candidate is not a Voter ('rejecting vote request since node is not a voter'), returning Granted false. Because the step-down precedes the rejection, a term-advancing vote request from an unelectable candidate still removes the receiver from leadership.
knowledge.conditions: Receiver is a Voter or Leader with a non-empty configurations.latest.Servers, and the candidate passes the inConfiguration check.

knowledge.statement: In appendEntries, when a received entry conflicts with one the node already stores, the node deletes the range [entry.Index, lastLogIdx] via logs.DeleteRange, then stores the replacement entries via logs.StoreLogs. If StoreLogs returns an error the handler logs 'failed to append to logs' and returns before any setLastLog call: the in-memory lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm keep the values they had before the deletion (the code marks this with a TODO), and no other branch in the receive path restores them. The response for that request is left with Success false.
knowledge.conditions: Follower/Candidate state; a.Term not older than the node's current term; at least one received entry whose index is at or below the node's last log index and whose term differs from the stored entry; and an error return from logs.StoreLogs for that call.

knowledge.statement: The in-memory last-log certificate is read through raftState.getLastEntry (and getLastIndex, which takes the maximum of lastLogIndex and lastSnapshotIndex, so a snapshot does not mask a stale log index). Its consumers are: electSelf and preElectSelf, which put it in RequestVoteRequest/RequestPreVoteRequest as LastLogIndex/LastLogTerm; requestVote/requestPreVote, which use it to decide whether to grant a vote; appendEntries, which compares it against PrevLogEntry to validate a leader's previous entry; and Raft.LastIndex, the public accessor. None of these consult the LogStore.
knowledge.conditions: Any node, whenever it campaigns or answers a vote request or validates an AppendEntries previous entry.

knowledge.statement: In the appendEntries entry loop the comparison 'entry.Index > lastLogIdx' uses lastLogIdx read from the in-memory certificate (getLastLog), not from the log store. For an entry at or below that cached index the handler calls logs.GetLog(entry.Index) and returns immediately if it errors, so once the conflicting suffix has been deleted from the store, any re-sent entry covering those indices makes the handler return before StoreLogs is reached. The certificate is never re-derived from the store inside this handler.
knowledge.conditions: Follower or Candidate state with at least one entry in the request whose index is at or below the cached last log index while that index is absent from the store (the state produced by a failed StoreLogs immediately after a conflicting-suffix deletion).

knowledge.statement: On an unsuccessful AppendEntries response the leader sets the peer's nextIndex to max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1), 1). When the follower's response carries a LastLog at or above the leader's index, the value settles at 1 (or at the floor) and the leader re-sends the same request, so a follower that rejects for a self-inflicted reason is re-driven with an identical request rather than a snapshot; ErrLogNotFound leading to SEND_SNAP is only produced from the leader's own log store, not from the follower's response.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; the follower responds Success=false with a LastLog hint at or above the leader's last index.

knowledge.statement: A single allowed error return from LogStore.StoreLogs in the call that follows a conflicting-suffix deletion leaves the follower unable to converge: its durable log keeps the truncated state (its last index falls to the last surviving index before the conflict), its cached last-log certificate keeps describing the deleted suffix, its commit and applied indexes stop advancing, and no further StoreLogs call is even attempted, so removing the error afterwards does not restore progress.
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter cluster over an in-memory transport, one follower holding an isolated uncommitted tail appended at an earlier term, a higher-term leader with committed replacement entries at the same indices, and exactly one allowed StoreLogs error on the replacement write; the fault may be removed afterwards without changing the outcome. In the observed run the same history with a healthy store converged inside the window (store 1..5, certificate (5,3), commit and applied 5) while the faulted node stayed at store last 2, certificate (4,2) and commit and applied 2 for 2.7 s.

knowledge.statement: When the wedged replica from the conflict-truncation store-error state is one of three voters, the cluster cannot commit any new entry after a single further voter loss: the leader accepts the entry into its own log (store and certificate advance to the new index) but its commit index stays at the value it had before and the client's apply future never completes, whereas the control run of the identical history without the store error commits the same entry as soon as the peer-loss phase begins. The wedged replica's store last index and StoreLogs attempt counter are unchanged across the phase, so its match index cannot advance and the quorum of match indexes can no longer include the new entry.
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter cluster over an in-memory transport; one voter left in the conflict-truncation store-error state (store truncated, cached certificate stale, no further store writes); one further voter removed; one client entry applied on the remaining leader. Observed for 1500 ms with 25 ms sampling, with the matching control run in the same execution.

knowledge.statement: appendConfigurationEntry dispatches the configuration entry and then, without waiting for it to commit, sets configurations.latest to the new configuration and calls leaderState.commitment.setConfiguration, which rebuilds the match-index map so that every voter of the new configuration is counted, with servers that have never answered starting at 0. The quorum decisions for commitment therefore use the new configuration from that moment, while configurations.committed still describes the old one.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; any successful configuration change request (AddVoter, AddNonvoter, DemoteVoter, RemoveServer) whose entry has been appended but not yet committed.

knowledge.statement: Both the leader lease check and the election path read configurations.latest, not the committed configuration: checkLeaderLease counts contacted voters of the latest configuration and demotes the leader when that count is below the latest configuration's quorum size, and quorumSize (used by candidates to decide when they have won) is computed from the same latest configuration. An uncommitted configuration whose quorum requires a server that never answers therefore both blocks commitment and removes the surviving servers' ability to keep or regain leadership.
knowledge.conditions: A node whose configurations.latest includes a voter added by a configuration entry that has not committed, while that voter is unreachable.

knowledge.statement: The timeout accepted by the configuration-change APIs bounds only the attempt to hand the request to the main loop: requestConfigChange returns errorFuture{ErrEnqueueTimeout} if the timer fires before the request is queued, otherwise it returns the future whose Error blocks until the configuration entry commits. A caller cannot use that timeout to learn that the configuration change is stuck.
knowledge.conditions: Any AddVoter/AddNonvoter/DemoteVoter/RemoveServer call with a non-zero timeout.
